## Oxford RECOVERY: The {{< var trial_cost_reduction_factor >}}× Proof

2020: British doctors cured COVID with a drug from 1961.
Cost: **{{< var recovery_trial_cost_per_patient >}} per patient**.

American pharma companies testing the same drugs under FDA rules: **{{< var traditional_phase3_cost_per_patient_fda_example_41k >}} per patient**.

## Switzerland: The 200-Year Peace Dividend

Two world wars.
Other nations fought.
Switzerland built wealth.

### Result

- [25% richer than Americans ($93K vs $76K GDP per capita)](references.qmd#swiss-vs-us-gdp-per-capita)
- Live [5 years longer (84 vs 79 years)](references.qmd#swiss-vs-us-life-expectancy)
- Haven't had a [war death since 1847](references.qmd#switzerland-last-war-death-1847)
- Military budget: [0.7% GDP](references.qmd#swiss-military-budget-0-7-pct-gdp) (US: {{< var us_military_spending_pct_gdp >}})

The difference went to education, healthcare, and trains that work.
Peace dividends compound over centuries.
War debts compound faster.

## War Bonds: How Capitalism Beat Fascism

WWII cost [$4 trillion (today's dollars)](references.qmd#wwii-cost-4-trillion-today).
America was broke.

**Solution:** Sell bonds to regular people.
Promise them profit and the defeat of fascism.

**Result:** [Funded the entire war](references.qmd#wwii-war-bonds), defeated fascism, everyone made money.

**The lesson:** When saving the world is profitable, people fund it.

[VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds](economics/victory-bonds-academic.qmd) use the same model.
Except instead of defeating fascism, the offer involves destroying cancer cells.

## The Landmine Treaty: Citizens Beat Armies

1992: Citizens decided landmines were awful.
1997: [160 countries banned them](references.qmd#icbl-ottawa-treaty).

No government started it.
No UN committee.
Just motivated citizens with fax machines.

They beat the entire military-industrial complex in 5 years with fax machines.

Society now has the internet.

## The Post-WW2 Economic Miracle: History's Greatest Peace Dividend

1945: US military spending [37% of GDP](references.qmd#us-post-wwii-military-spending-cut) (highest in history).
1948: Cut to [7% of GDP](references.qmd#us-post-wwii-military-spending-cut) (30 percentage points redirected).

**Result:** The greatest economic boom in human history.

- GDP growth: **[8% average](references.qmd#us-post-wwii-gdp-growth-8-pct)** for a decade (vs 2-3% normal)
- Middle class explosion: [Home ownership doubled](references.qmd#us-post-wwii-home-ownership-doubled)
- Education boom: GI Bill created modern knowledge economy
- Infrastructure: Interstate highway system built

**The lesson:** Redirecting military spending to productive uses equals a prosperity explosion.

## The Political Precedents: Strategies for Success

### Creating Binding International Law

**The Precedent: The International Campaign to Ban Landmines (ICBL)**

Citizens created international law with fax machines.

- The ICBL got 160 nations to ban landmines through peer pressure and shame.
- No government started it. Citizens did.
- It worked in 5 years.

**The Lesson:** Citizens with fax machines beat the military-industrial complex. Modern tools include social media. The **[Global Referendum](strategy/strategy-execution-overview-academic.qmd)** leverages these precedents.

### Achieving a Political Tipping Point

**The Precedent: The {{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}} Rule (Erica Chenoweth's Research)**

Harvard researchers analyzed revolutions. They found the necessary threshold: {{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}}.

- Once {{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}} of any population actively protests something, it wins. Always.
- Civil rights: Won at {{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}}
- Indian independence: Won at {{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}}
- Failed movements: Never hit {{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}}

**The Lesson:** Universal participation is unnecessary. The movement needs {{< var treaty_campaign_voting_bloc_target >}} million people out of {{< var global_population_2024 >}} billion. That represents one person in every classroom, one family on every block.

## The Financial Precedents: Funding Mechanisms

### Mobilizing Mass Public Capital

#### The Precedent: WWII War Bonds

Americans funded the defeat of fascism by buying bonds. They made money while saving democracy.

- War Bonds raised trillions (today's dollars)
- Regular people bought them to defeat fascism and get 3% returns
- It worked

**The Lesson:** **[VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds](economics/economics-academic.qmd)** copy the formula. Except instead of defeating fascism for 3%, participants kill cancer for 271%.

### B. Building a New Global Health Institution

**The Precedent: The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria**

The idea of creating a new, multi-billion-dollar global health institution from scratch has been done before.

- The Global Fund was created in 2002 as a public-private partnership to pool and distribute billions of dollars to fight these three diseases, operating outside of traditional institutional channels. It has since saved an estimated [70 million lives](references.qmd#global-fund-50-million-lives-saved) (as of 2025).

**The Lesson:** This provides the precedent for **[a decentralized institutes of health (DIH)](solution/dih-academic.qmd).**
It proves that the world is capable of creating new, large-scale, and more efficient financial institutions for global health when the existing systems are insufficient.

### C. Pricing the Political Risk

**The Precedent: Michael Milken's High-Yield Bonds & George Soros's Political Arbitrage**

The investment thesis for VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds, a high-risk, high-reward bet on a political outcome, is grounded in proven financial strategies.

- **Michael Milken** proved that to attract capital for high-risk ventures, the issuer must offer a correspondingly high, contractually obligated return.
- **George Soros's** legendary bet against the British pound in 1992 serves as an example of privately financed political arbitrage, proving it is possible to deploy immense private capital to bet on a political outcome.

**The Lesson:** The financial model, which offers a **$>{{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} targeted return**, is a direct application of these principles.
It correctly prices the political risk to attract the sophisticated capital needed to win.

## 4. The Cautionary Tales: Avoiding Failure

The failures of past movements are even more instructive than the successes, as they reveal the exact failure modes the strategy is engineered to avoid.

### A. Moral Arguments Require Financial Support

**The Precedent: The Nuclear Disarmament Movement ("The Freeze")**

- **The Failure:** Despite enormous popular support in the 1980s, the movement largely failed because it could not overcome the entrenched financial interests of the military-industrial complex.
- **The Lesson:** This offers historical proof for the core thesis: **Good intentions alone cannot defeat bad money.** It acts as the primary justification for the strategy of **["legal bribery"](strategy/strategy-execution-overview-academic.qmd)** and co-opting opposition with a superior financial offer.

### B. Avoid Diffuse Goals

#### The Precedent: Occupy Wall Street

- **The Failure:** While it successfully changed the public conversation in 2011, the movement produced no lasting policy change because it lacked a single, specific, actionable demand.
- **The Lesson:** The project avoids this trap by focusing all energy and capital on a single, clear, and achievable goal: **ratification of a "[1% treaty](solution/1-percent-treaty-academic.qmd)."** That is the only ask.
